clinical_knowledge.topic: Latex Allergy (IgE-mediated contact urticaria) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Latex Allergy (IgE-mediated contact urticaria) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Latex Allergy: Switch to nitrile gloves, avoid latex products, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: itchy hives on hands after wearing latex gloves

Key HPI features: A 56-year-old female presents to the clinic with itchy hives on hands after wearing latex gloves. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Latex Allergy.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Latex Allergy (IgE-mediated contact urticaria).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Irritant contact dermatitis (from glove powder/friction) without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Any systemic symptoms — hives beyond the hands, breathing trouble — signal a risk of full anaphylaxis on future exposure.
management_principles: Plan for Latex Allergy: Switch to nitrile gloves, avoid latex products
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with chief complaint of itchy hives on hands after wearing latex gloves. HPI: IgE-mediated latex protein allergy.
reference_soap.objective: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Latex Allergy.
reference_soap.assessment: Condition highly suspicious for Latex Allergy.
reference_soap.plan: Plan for Latex Allergy: Switch to nitrile gloves, avoid latex products. Consult specialist if symptoms worsen. Counsel patient.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Latex Allergy
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Latex Allergy
Implement evidence-based management plan: Switch to nitrile gloves, avoid latex products

teaching.one_liner: An IgE-mediated reaction to latex proteins causing hives at the point of contact — commonly the hands after wearing latex gloves — with a risk of cross-reaction to certain fruits.
differentials: Allergic contact dermatitis (Type IV, to rubber chemical additives)
red_flags: Any systemic symptoms — hives beyond the hands, breathing trouble — signal a risk of full anaphylaxis on future exposure

must_ask.say: How soon after putting on the gloves did your hands react?

must_ask.objective: Location and character of the reaction
must_ask.say: Is it just hives on your hands, or does it involve anywhere else?
Do you wear latex gloves regularly for work?
Do you have any reactions to bananas, avocado, or kiwi?
Have you ever had swelling or breathing trouble from latex, not just skin symptoms?
